title: Now Entering: The Era Of Bleh | NOEMA
gist: Horwath argues that indiscriminate 'AI for everything' adoption makes competitors effectively share one brain ('Airbrain'), homogenizing output and eroding differentiation and worker skills. He predicts a bifurcation of knowledge work into cheap AI output with offshored human-in-the-loop oversight versus a premium human 'tastemaker' tier, plus a failed fractional/gig experiment.

insights.claim: When every company in an industry runs its knowledge work through the same small ecosystem of LLMs, it is as if they all hired the same single employee, eroding competitive differentiation.
insights.speaker: AARON HORWATH
insights.so_what: Firms whose moat is knowledge-work differentiation (agencies, consulting, marketing) face margin compression from AI-driven sameness.
insights.quote: Almost as if all these companies have simultaneously hired the same single employee: Mr. Claude (or one of his contemporaries).

insights.claim: Wenger and Kenett tested 22 commercial LLMs against over 100 humans on creativity tasks and found individual models sometimes beat individuals, but LLMs as a population converged on strikingly similar answers while humans did not.
insights.speaker: AARON HORWATH
insights.so_what: Empirical basis that AI outputs are correlated across vendors, undermining AI as a differentiation source.
insights.quote: But as a population, the LLMs converged on strikingly similar answers, while the humans didn’t.
insights.locator: This inevitability should not be surprising.

insights.claim: Newsletters, websites and ads across competitors are converging on the same Claude-aesthetic and tone, analogous to the social-media-driven 'AirSpace' homogenization of cafes described by Kyle Chayka.
insights.speaker: AARON HORWATH
insights.so_what: Expect a premium on distinctive brand voice and human-made content as AI output saturates.
insights.quote: Newsletters, websites and ads across competitors and industries are converging on the same Claude-aesthetic, the same tone of voice and the same way of articulating ideas.

insights.claim: Jay Barney and co-authors argue AI can offer at best a short-term competitive advantage because whatever value it unlocks is unlocked for all, making it a source of homogenization rather than differentiation.
insights.speaker: AARON HORWATH
insights.so_what: AI adoption is table stakes, not alpha; don't reward companies for AI adoption alone.
insights.quote: Far from being a source of differentiation, artificial intelligence will be a source of homogenization.
insights.locator: In his MIT Sloan Management Review

insights.claim: AI is shifting from producing content to shaping strategy, sales coaching, campaign strategy and stakeholder management, the foundational tasks that define a company's direction and market perception.
insights.speaker: AARON HORWATH
insights.so_what: Homogenization risk extends to strategy, not just marketing output.
insights.locator: But AI isn’t only generating Workslop.

insights.claim: At an AI-first SaaS company described in the piece, executives expect a copywriter not to write at all but to manage agents, and the team has downsized while his scope widened.
insights.speaker: AARON HORWATH
insights.so_what: Illustrates AI-driven headcount reduction and role expansion in mid-sized SaaS.
insights.quote: “The expectation from our executives is I shouldn’t write at all,” says Weber

insights.claim: The Kissimmee River straightening (1962-1971) stopped flooding but destroyed ~35,000 acres of floodplain habitat and ~90% of wintering waterfowl, and restoring 44 miles of bends cost over $1 billion, a parable for removing the 'inefficient' bends in knowledge work.
insights.speaker: AARON HORWATH
insights.so_what: Over-optimizing workflows can incur large, delayed remediation costs.
insights.quote: The project wrapped in 2021 and cost more than $1 billion.

insights.claim: AI-enabled solo execution eliminates the meetings and stakeholder feedback loops that refined ideas, turning knowledge work into something like manufacturing with humans as foremen, which is hostile to innovation.
insights.speaker: AARON HORWATH
insights.so_what: Heavy-AI organizations may see falling innovation output despite higher volume.
insights.quote: The result is a transformation of knowledge work into something more akin to manufacturing, with humans operating as the foremen keeping an eye on the metaphorical assembly line.

insights.claim: An organization's unique selling points are the aggregate talents of its people, and routing all work through AI filters out the talent firms pay for.
insights.speaker: AARON HORWATH
insights.so_what: Talent-dense firms that protect human judgment may retain pricing power.
insights.quote: Building an organization with the right combination of people is, and always has been, the ultimate moat.

insights.claim: Rory Sutherland's 'doorman fallacy' explains why cost-cutting automation of a role's notional task misses hidden value such as relationships, trust and status signaling.
insights.speaker: AARON HORWATH
insights.so_what: Automation-driven cost savings may be overstated where roles carry unpriced value.
insights.quote: The doorman may actually increase what you can charge for a night’s stay in your hotel.

insights.claim: A 2026 Nature report found skills atrophy very quickly once AI is introduced, and in a 2026 survey of 2,500 employees 39% said AI reliance was making them less intelligent.
insights.speaker: AARON HORWATH
insights.so_what: Firms reversing AI-heavy workflows will face a costly ramp to rebuild human capability.
insights.quote: In a 2026 survey of 2,500 employees, 39% said their reliance on AI was actively making them less intelligent.
insights.locator: There’s a reason for urgency here

insights.claim: Organizations quickest to adopt AI without limits should prepare for a more targeted approach, in some cases rebuilding human-driven processes.
insights.speaker: AARON HORWATH
insights.so_what: Expect a correction phase in enterprise AI adoption toward selective use.

insights.claim: In cafes, once algorithms made venues interchangeable (only 6% of test participants could tell Chicago from San Francisco cafes by photo), sameness stopped paying and differentiated experiences became the premium.
insights.speaker: AARON HORWATH
insights.so_what: Precedent for a market swing back toward differentiation after tech-driven convergence.
insights.quote: when asked to distinguish Chicago from San Francisco, only 6% succeeded

insights.claim: Once every player in an industry uses AI, its advantage is neutralized and firms will return to seeking humans for uniqueness in content, strategy and solutions.
insights.speaker: AARON HORWATH
insights.so_what: Human judgment and taste become the scarce, priced input in AI-saturated markets.
insights.quote: Once every player in an industry is leveraging AI, any competitive advantage it offers is neutralized

insights.claim: Deloitte's 2026 Global Human Capital Trends report says competitive advantage now comes more from cultivating the human edge, and EY committed $100 million to reward employees for adaptability, innovation and judgment.
insights.speaker: AARON HORWATH
insights.so_what: Large professional-services firms are reallocating spend toward human differentiation.
insights.quote: Technology — especially something as increasingly ubiquitous as AI — is replicable. People aren’t.
insights.locator: The big geese in consulting agree.

insights.claim: Successful firms will deliberately designate AI-free areas and distinguish friction worth eliminating from friction that produces the best work.
insights.speaker: AARON HORWATH
insights.so_what: Operational AI strategy, not blanket adoption, will separate winners.

insights.claim: McGurk and Khachaturov describe a barbell in AI-saturated markets: near-zero-marginal-cost AI output at one pole and verifiably human products at a premium at the other, with the middle hollowing out.
insights.speaker: AARON HORWATH
insights.so_what: Mid-market knowledge-work businesses face squeeze; human-provenance verification may become infrastructure.
insights.quote: Most importantly, the middle will hollow out.

insights.claim: Human-in-the-loop oversight roles will mostly shift to lower-cost labor markets because checking homogenized AI output does not justify premium pay.
insights.speaker: AARON HORWATH
insights.so_what: Bullish for offshore BPO/oversight labor; bearish for onshore mid-level knowledge-work wages.
insights.quote: What sense does it make to pay a premium for oversight when a worker with clear instructions and a Claude account can produce or evaluate that same, homogenized output for a fraction of the cost?

insights.claim: AI labs themselves signal this shift: Anthropic is hiring highly paid tastemakers and ChatGPT is hiring an Employer Brand Manager, while developer, designer and PM roles are being combined into a single builder role.
insights.speaker: AARON HORWATH
insights.so_what: Role consolidation implies fewer total tech jobs and higher pay for a smaller taste-defining tier.
insights.quote: Anthropic is hiring highly paid tastemakers, inoculating itself against the very airbrain it’s creating.
insights.locator: If there’s any doubt about this

insights.claim: A small group of tastemakers will capture a growing share of the salary pie, mirroring the broader wealth gap, as knowledge work becomes ruthlessly bifurcated.
insights.speaker: AARON HORWATH
insights.so_what: Points to widening wage inequality within white-collar work.
insights.quote: The future of knowledge work, then, will be ruthlessly bifurcated.

insights.claim: Executives will be tempted by spreadsheets showing ~70% salary reductions to try an Uber-like fractional model for knowledge work.
insights.speaker: AARON HORWATH
insights.so_what: Gig/freelance platforms could benefit from a corporate shift to fractional labor.
insights.quote: Oh, those spreadsheets with 70% reductions in salaries will be tantalizing.

insights.claim: Upwork's Future of Work Index 2026 reports skilled freelancing rose from 28% of skilled knowledge workers in 2025 to 38% in 2026, and Gartner predicts over 30% of midsize enterprises will have a fractional executive on retainer by 2027.
insights.speaker: AARON HORWATH
insights.so_what: Rapid freelance growth is a tailwind for freelance marketplaces like Upwork.
insights.quote: skilled freelancing rose from 28% of skilled knowledge workers in 2025 to 38% in 2026

insights.claim: The AI-plus-gig-economy model will fail long-term because an organization of overwhelmingly fractional workers isn't an organization, but only after disrupting lives and gutting businesses.
insights.speaker: AARON HORWATH
insights.so_what: Near-term cost-cutting wins may reverse; watch for firms that over-fractionalize.
insights.quote: But also because an organization composed of overwhelmingly fractional workers isn’t an organization at all.
insights.locator: In the near future, LinkedIn feeds
